newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia unveils future privatisation plans.
newsitem.headline: Latvia unveils future privatisation plans.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) unveiled its 1997 and 1998 plans on Wednesday, saying it wanted to sell some 320 state enterprises over the next two years.
It said it would continue to privatise the big energy and transport firms and sell 29 companies via the stock exchange.
"We have to contribute 30 to 32 million lats to the privatisation fund (budget) and one million to the fund of local municipalities," LPA chief Janis Naglis told a news conference.
Latvian Shipping, Latvian Gas, electricity supplier Latvenergo and oil terminal Ventspils Nafta are some of the biggest Latvian companies on the privatisation list.
"Some 90 percent of state assets have been handed over for privatisation since 1994," Naglis added.
A total 14 potential investors have applied to take part in the sale of 30 to 35 percent of the Latvian Shipping Company, which the LPA says is the world's 19th largest shipping company.
"Seven of them (potential investors) are shipping companies and six are investment funds," Naglis said.
One U.S., one Latvian, six British and three Scandinavian companies are among those who have expressed their interest in Latvian Shipping and the agency is scheduling meetings with candidates now.
The delayed privatisation agreement for Latvian Gas is expected to be signed by the end of February with both Russian Gazprom and the German Preussen/Ruhrgas consortium, he said.
He said that the audit was underway for Latvenergo, bids for which have already been invited and which has also attracted German, Swedish and Finnish interest.
